In [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") there is no difference between _town_ ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Stadt_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _ville(s)_[Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): _città_ _city_ ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Grossstadt_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _grande ville(s)_[Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): _metropoli_
Below is a list of [towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town "Town") and [cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City "City") in Switzerland. Until 2014 [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality "Municipality") with more than 10,000 inhabitants were considered to be towns. Since 2014, the [Federal Statistical Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Statistical_Office_\(Switzerland\) "Federal Statistical Office \(Switzerland\)") (FSO) uses a new algorithm (called [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Statistische Städte 2012_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Villes statistiques 2012_[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Switzerland#cite_note-1) Currently, FSO considers 162 municipalities as towns/cities ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Statistische Städte_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Villes statistiques_[German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Gemeinde_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _commune_[Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): _comune_[municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_of_Switzerland "Municipalities of Switzerland").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Switzerland#cite_note-publ-2): 14–19 
## List of towns and cities
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_cities_in_Switzerland&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: List of towns and cities")]
This is an alphabetical list of towns or cities (these English terms can be used interchangeably, as there is no official differentiation), which follows the FSO's definition ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Statistische Städte 2012_[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Villes statistiques 2012_[town rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_privileges "Town privileges") (h) and/or [market towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_town "Market town") (m).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Switzerland#cite_note-publ-2): 14–19 
  * Places in **bold print** are towns because of the FSO's definition _and_ historic town/market rights.
  * Places in _italics_ are towns excluded by the FSO's definition, but places which have either historic town rights (h) or historic market rights (m).
  * Places in normal print are towns according to the FSO's definition.
  * Places that had lost historic town rights previously are identified with "-h".
